New endpoints GET /api/v1/release/changelog (serves the embedded CHANGELOG.md parsed by version, Unreleased excluded) and GET /api/v1/release/latest (returns the latest GitHub release tag with a 1 h server-side cache; 204 when GitHub is unreachable so the card renders a clean offline state). Version comparison normalises the leading v so a daemon reporting 2026.05.02 matches a GitHub tag like v2026.05.02. CHANGELOG.md is embedded into the binary via //go:embed at build time (the Makefile and Ansible build role copy the repo-root file into the embed location; the copy is gitignored to keep the repo root the single source of truth).
  • Run-level retry policy. Failed runs now schedule themselves for automatic retry up to a configurable cap before going permanently failed. Settings exposes a global default (max retries + JSON delays array, defaults 2 and [900,3600,14400] seconds → 15 min / 1 h / 4 h). Each job can override both fields in the wizard's Advanced step. A new scheduler watcher runs @every 1m, atomically claims rows whose retry_next_at has expired, and dispatches via a new RunJobRetry(jobID, originalRunID, attempt) path. Triggers retries on: stall cancellation, pre-flight failure, encryption-config error, pre-script failure, panic recovery, and terminal failed status. Suppresses retries when the destination breaker is open, when the run was operator-cancelled, or when the run was a manual "run now" (the API/MCP "run now" callers now route through RunJobManual so they don't auto-retry).
  • Pre-flight destination check. Every scheduled run runs a fast TestConnection (15 s ceiling) against the destination before opening the backup pipeline. Unreachable destinations now produce a skipped job_run row with a clear reason instead of consuming the 4-hour job timeout. The skip counts toward the circuit breaker so a chronically unreachable destination eventually opens its breaker.
  • Per-destination circuit breaker. Each storage destination tracks consecutive_failures and a breaker_state (closed / open). The breaker opens after 3 consecutive failures (job runs OR daily health checks OR preflight) and auto-closes after 2 consecutive successes. While open, scheduled runs targeting the destination skip with a clear reason instead of failing. New POST /api/v1/storage/{id}/breaker/close endpoint resets the breaker manually (204). Storage page shows a "Breaker open" badge with the timestamp tooltip and a "Reset breaker" button when the breaker is open. Encryption/pre-script failures and operator cancellations intentionally do NOT count against the breaker (they're config issues, not destination health).
  • Heartbeat file at /var/local/vault/heartbeat (hybrid mode) or alongside vault.db. Refreshed every 30 s with <RFC3339 timestamp> v<version> so external monitoring (Unraid notifications, monit, custom watchdog) can detect a hung daemon by checking the file mtime. RAM-backed in hybrid mode so it doesn't wear flash. Write failures are logged at most once per hour to avoid log spam.
  • Graceful drain on SIGTERM. Daemon shutdown now waits up to 30 s for the active backup to finish at the next per-file boundary before tearing down the HTTP server. After the drain ceiling fires, the existing context-cancel still terminates mid-flight work. New Runner.Drain(ctx) API; runner refuses new RunJob invocations once draining.
  • Encrypted offsite database backup with fan-out. The post-backup DB copy now (a) runs PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) so the on-disk file is self-contained, (b) encrypts with the global passphrase when one is configured (writes age-format .age; plaintext + warning log otherwise), (c) writes both a timestamped historical copy (_vault/vault.db.YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SS.age) and a stable _vault/vault.db.latest.age pointer, and (d) fans out to every destination flagged "Include in DB backup" in addition to the job's own destination. New backup_database_enabled column on storage_destinations (default off). Storage page exposes the toggle as "Include in DB backup".
  • Rolling snapshot history (keep last 7). After every successful primary snapshot save, the file is also copied to <snapshot_dir>/rotated/vault.db.YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SS.nanos and the rotated directory is pruned to the 7 newest entries. Uses a hardlink on the same filesystem (zero extra bytes for unchanged snapshots) and falls back to a byte copy on cross-device errors. Filenames use UTC dashes-only timestamps with nanosecond resolution so they sort chronologically and never collide. Rotation failures are logged but never block the snapshot pipeline, so a transient disk issue cannot poison the main save path.
  • Per-destination deduplication (opt-in). Storage destinations gain an "Enable deduplication" toggle (immutable after creation). When enabled, folder, plugin, and container-volume backups to that destination are content-defined-chunked, encrypted per-chunk, and packed so identical data across snapshots, jobs, and containers is stored once. VM, ZFS, and flash backups continue to use the classic tar pipeline. The Storage card shows the dedup ratio, chunk/pack counts, reclaimable bytes (the space a cleanup could reclaim, measured at the last GC and persisted in a new dedup_gc_runs table so the figure and last-cleanup time survive daemon restarts and are visible from any request – they no longer read 0), and a "Run cleanup" button. "Run cleanup" now also compacts mixed packs (those above a configurable dead-bytes threshold): live chunks are copied verbatim into fresh packs (no decrypt/re-encrypt – chunk encryption is deterministic and keyed by content ID, so the on-disk bytes are identical regardless of which pack holds them), chunks are atomically re-pointed in the DB, and the old packs are tombstoned + deleted. Chunks remain readable from at least one pack at every observable step. The threshold lives in Settings → General as "Compaction threshold (% dead bytes)" (key dedup_compaction_min_dead_ratio, default 0.5 = 50%; set to 100 to disable compaction). The on-storage _vault/index/*.idx log gained a tombstone record + last-writer-wins rebuild semantics so vault dedup repair correctly removes deleted packs (and re-points moved chunks) during a disaster-recovery rebuild – closes a latent bug where the rebuild path would resurrect packs that GC had deleted. GC's sweep also now reaps empty packs (created if a compaction crashes between writing the new pack and re-pointing chunks) so any orphan from a partial compaction self-cleans on the next run. The dedup_gc_runs table gained compacted_packs and reclaimed_bytes columns; both surface in the dedup_gc_complete WebSocket payload and the daemon log line. New endpoints GET /api/v1/storage/{id}/dedup-stats and POST /api/v1/storage/{id}/gc. New CLI subcommands vault dedup repair --dest=<id> (rebuild the SQLite index from on-storage data after DB loss) and vault dedup gc --dest=<id>; both accept a --key flag to read vault.key from a non-default location (e.g. a disaster-recovery restore where the key was placed beside a copied database). Quick + deep verify both work on dedup restore points without UI changes.
  • Restore wizard file picker. The restore wizard's summary step now has a "Restore specific files…" disclosure per item. Pick individual files (or whole subtrees) with a path filter, select-all, and clear. Items left untouched still restore in full. Falls back to whole-archive extract for backups produced before partial restore shipped.
  • Partial restore via tar index sidecar. Folder, plugin, and container-volume backups now write a small index sidecar (<archive>.index.json) next to each tar archive listing every entry. The restore API accepts an optional file_paths map so only the named entries are extracted (descendants of selected directories are included automatically). Sidecars are encrypted alongside the archive when the job uses encryption. Pre-existing backups continue to restore everything via the legacy whole-archive path.
  • Grandfather-father-son (GFS) retention. New optional keep_latest, keep_daily, keep_weekly, keep_monthly, keep_yearly fields per job (all default 0 = disabled). When any are set, the runner keeps the newest N latest plus the first restore point per day/week/month/year bucket. A single restore point can fill several buckets at once. Existing retention_count / retention_days are unchanged and continue to apply on every other job. Chain-ancestor protection still applies so kept incrementals always have a restorable parent.
  • GFS retention preview in the Jobs wizard. As users tune the keep counts, the wizard shows "Would keep X of Y current restore points · Z would be pruned" 300 ms after the last keystroke. Backed by a new GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/retention-preview endpoint. Hidden for new jobs that don't have restore points yet.
  • Restore-point verification with quick and deep modes. POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/restore-points/{rpid}/verify queues a verify run and returns a verify_run_id; progress streams over the WebSocket. Quick stats every recorded file and fails on missing files or size mismatches (no data transfer, suitable for weekly scheduled runs). Deep streams every file and re-checks SHA-256 against the backup-time manifest – catches silent bit rot on cold storage. Two helper endpoints round out the API (GET .../verify-runs/{vrid} and GET .../restore-points/{rpid}/verify-runs). Verify runs in its own goroutine and does not block scheduled backups.
  • Scheduled verification per job. Two new job columns (verify_schedule, verify_mode) let you run quick or deep verify on its own cadence, independent of the backup schedule (e.g. nightly backups + weekly deep verify). Configured in the wizard's Advanced step via the same friendly day/time picker used for the backup schedule; no cron expertise required.
  • Daily storage destination health check. The scheduler runs TestConnection against every destination at 03:30 local (deliberately after typical backup windows so a failing destination is caught before the next morning's run). Results persist on the destination row and broadcast over the WebSocket. The Storage page shows a Healthy / Unhealthy badge with the error in the tooltip. POST /api/v1/storage/{id}/health-check triggers an on-demand check.
  • Orphan file GC (dry-run by default). POST /api/v1/storage/{id}/scan-orphans lists files on a destination that don't belong to any active restore point. Safe to call repeatedly; no state changes. POST /api/v1/storage/{id}/delete-orphans deletes specified paths after re-scanning to ensure each is still orphaned. Useful for reclaiming quota on managed providers after failed runs. UI is API-only in v1.
  • Per-destination bandwidth throttling. Optional bandwidth_limit_mbps field on every non-local storage config caps upload + download throughput (megabits per second). Default 0 = unlimited. Metadata operations (List/Stat/Delete/TestConnection) are never throttled. Exposed in the Storage form as a single "Bandwidth limit (Mbps)" input.
  • Configurable S3 multipart part size (part_size_mb). Default 0 uses 64 MiB parts (640 GB per-object ceiling, fits typical home-server workloads). Raise to 256, 512, or 1024 MiB for very large datasets (up to 10 TB). Range is enforced at 5–5120 MiB per the S3 protocol. Peak upload memory ≈ part_size × concurrency (default 5), so 1 GiB parts cost roughly 5 GiB of RAM during active uploads.
  • Configurable WebDAV chunk size (chunk_size_mb). Default 0 uses 50 MiB chunks. Positive values set the chunk size in MiB. Negative values disable chunking but keep memory-safe known-length writes.
  • Automatic compression downgrade for media-heavy backups. Folder, plugin, and container-volume backups now sample the source up-front and, when ≥ 70% of the bytes have already-compressed file extensions (.mp4, .mkv, .flac, .jpg, .zip, .gz, .zst, …), automatically drop the requested gzip/zstd compression to none for that archive. A 200 GB Immich library or a Jellyfin folder no longer wastes CPU re-compressing already-compressed bytes. The decision is logged and the manifest records the compression actually used so restore continues to auto-detect via magic bytes.
  • Diagnostics bundle captures the daemon log, per-job item settings, storage health-check trend, runtime settings, and disk space. Every bug we triaged in recent QA was diagnosed by reading the daemon log, inspecting per-job item settings, or checking storage health history – none of which were in the previous bundle. The collector now tees daemon output through a 1 MiB in-memory ring buffer at startup and includes the redacted snapshot as vault.log in the ZIP. Each job's items are included with redacted settings (exclusion paths, container ID, mount info, ZFS dataset, etc.) so support reports show which items were configured and how. Storage destinations include their dedup state and last health-check result. A credential-free settings snapshot reports things like which categories are enabled, whether an API key is set, and the configured staging/snapshot overrides. Disk usage is probed for /boot, /tmp, /var/local/vault, the DB directory, the staging dir, and every discovered Unraid pool. Run history is split into a structured log + extracted error messages instead of one stuffed field. Activity entries now include category and details. A new redactor scrubs Authorization, X-API-Key, Cookie/Set-Cookie, Proxy-Authorization, AWS sigv4 Credential=, JSON/query-string credential fields, inline URL credentials, and Discord webhook tokens from the log tail before it's embedded.
  • Diagnostics also captures verify-run history, per-destination dedup stats, runtime metrics, pool discovery, Docker / libvirt connectivity, and scheduler state. New ZIP entries: verify_runs.json (last 25 quick + deep runs), dedup_stats.json (per dedup destination), runtime.json (goroutines, heap, GC, uptime), pools.json (every discovered Unraid pool with its mount status), connectivity.json (Docker socket + libvirt URI probes; errors are captured so "Docker not reachable" is itself the diagnostic), scheduler.json (next-run timestamp per enabled job).
  • Diagnostics ZIP layout is split into per-section files instead of one fat diagnostics.json. Support engineers can now unzip -p bundle.zip jobs.json | jq without paging through unrelated sections. The top-level diagnostics.json is a one-screen overview that omits activity, runs, and the log tail.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• SaveSnapshot now runs PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) before invoking the SQLite Online Backup API so the resulting snapshot file is self-contained and the WAL is reclaimed on disk. Checkpoint failures are logged but never block the snapshot. New PRAGMA journal_size_limit = 67108864 (64 MiB) at every Open() bounds the WAL between checkpoints.
  • restoreWithFallback runs PRAGMA integrity_check on every successfully-restored tier and falls through to the next tier (primary → default cache → USB backup → fresh DB) when the check fails. A corrupt snapshot can no longer silently become the working database – at worst the daemon starts with a fresh DB and tells the operator to reconfigure.
  • HTTP API shutdown now drains the runner for up to 30 s before the existing 5 s HTTP Shutdown window. A planned restart (plugin upgrade) lets the active per-file upload reach the next boundary instead of being killed mid-stream. After the drain ceiling fires, the existing context-cancel path still tears down mid-flight work. New Runner.Drain(ctx) is the API surface.
  • job_runs.status can now be skipped. Two paths produce skipped runs: a pre-flight check failing to reach the destination, and a scheduled run firing against an open breaker. The History page renders skipped rows neutrally (not red), and the deferred retry watcher picks up preflight-skipped rows for re-attempt.
  • Bandwidth limit no longer offered for local storage destinations. Throttling local I/O slowed backups for no operational benefit. The Storage form hides the field for local destinations and the factory ignores any stale value left in an older config. SFTP, SMB, NFS, WebDAV, and S3 continue to honour the limit.
  • Restore wizard, History timeline, Logs, and Dashboard Recent Activity now show absolute timestamps as the primary label, with the relative form (48m ago) preserved as a hover tooltip. Matches how Veeam, restic, and Time Machine present restore points (closes #81).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Editing any field on a storage destination no longer silently corrupts the saved password. The Settings → Edit Storage modal pre-fills its password input with whatever the API returned ("••••••••" for any destination with credentials – the redaction marker). Saving the form without retyping the password posted that marker back to PUT /api/v1/storage/{id}, which the server then stored verbatim as the new password, causing every subsequent backup/test to 401. PUT /storage/{id} now runs the incoming config through preserveRedactedSecrets: any sensitiveConfigKey whose value equals the "••••••••" marker is rewritten to the corresponding value from the previously-stored config before persistence. New typed credentials still overwrite as before. The fix is server-side because the trap affected the UI modal AND any other client (MCP tools, ansible automation, direct API scripts) round-tripping a partial edit.
  • S3 destinations no longer fail with Head "//<bucket>./<endpoint>": unsupported protocol scheme "" when the operator pasted a bare-hostname endpoint (e.g. s3.us-east-005.backblazeb2.com, exactly as Backblaze B2's web console displays it). The adapter handed the unmodified string to the AWS SDK, where url.Parse left Host empty and the virtual-host-style bucket-prefix resolver emitted a malformed URL with no scheme. NewS3Adapter now runs every endpoint through normalizeS3Endpoint: bare hostnames are promoted to https://…, schemes other than http(s) are rejected at construction time, and parsed URLs with an empty host are rejected. TestConnection-style checks and previously-stored destinations are unaffected once the daemon restarts. The same constructor now also TrimSpaces access_key and secret_key to defend against the related copy-paste failure where stray whitespace from the B2 console produced a 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch with no obvious cause.
  • WebDAV chunked uploads to Nextcloud (and other Sabre/DAV servers) no longer fail with WriteStreamWithLength …/000000.part: 400. The WebDAV adapter wrote each chunk of a logical-file upload as <index>.part inside the .chunks sidecar directory. Nextcloud's default forbidden_filename_extensions / blacklisted_files_regex reserves .part and .filepart for its own in-progress-upload mechanism and rejects external PUTs to those names with HTTP 400 Bad Request. Single-PUT uploads (small backups, < 50 MiB) were unaffected, so TestConnection and small jobs passed while every chunked container backup failed on the first chunk. Chunk files are now written with a .dat suffix, which is not on any known WebDAV server blacklist. The fix is forward-only safe: every chunk's absolute path is recorded in the manifest, so historical restore points continue to read correctly from their original .part chunks. writeChunked's cleanup path also now removes the (empty) .chunks collection when a chunked upload aborts on the first chunk, so failures leave nothing behind on the remote.
  • Dedup ratio and logical-bytes stats are correct for multi-item dedup destinations. The Storage card's dedup ratio showed 0× / 0 B → N (and the diagnostics bundle reported zero logical bytes) for any destination fed by a multi-item job – e.g. a containers dedup backup. DedupAggregates summed restore_points.size_bytes only WHERE manifest_id IS NOT NULL, but that column is set only for single-item jobs; multi-item jobs leave it NULL and store per-item IDs in metadata.item_manifests, so their logical bytes were excluded entirely. The query now sums every restore point for the destination's jobs (the destination is already known to be dedup-enabled and dedup mode is immutable per destination), so the ratio reflects real savings.
  • GC no longer deletes live data from large container/plugin dedup backups. A container's dedup manifest references its volume file data only indirectly: each __vol__<dest> entry points at a sub-manifest, which lists the actual data chunks. GC's reachability set (collectLiveManifestIDs, used by both the daemon's POST /storage/{id}/gc and the vault dedup gc CLI) collected only the top-level manifest IDs, and GC marks just the direct chunks of each live manifest – so the volume data chunks were never marked. Any pack containing only such chunks (i.e. every data-only pack of a backup larger than one 24 MiB pack) was swept, silently corrupting the backup; the next restore would fail with missing chunks. The live set is now expanded through a new engine.WalkManifestClosure that recurses into volume sub-manifests, so every reachable chunk is marked. Folder/plugin single-level backups were unaffected; small single-pack container backups happened to survive because their data shared a pack with a manifest chunk. Confirmed with a multi-pack regression test.
  • Deep and quick verify now work on multi-item dedup restore points and actually re-hash container volume data. Verify keyed off restore_points.manifest_id, which is only set for single-item dedup jobs; a multi-item job (e.g. a containers backup) stores per-item IDs under metadata.item_manifests and leaves manifest_id empty, so verify fell through to the classic per-file path and failed with "no recorded file checksums in restore point metadata". Verify now detects a dedup restore point from either source, walks every item's manifest closure (including the nested volume sub-manifests), and in deep mode re-reads + re-hashes every leaf data chunk – previously even a single-item container deep verify only checked the top-level manifest's pointer chunks, not the file data. Quick mode stats the unique packs across the full closure.
  • Dedup (chunked) backups now honour container/folder path exclusions, matching the classic tar pipeline. ContainerHandler.BackupChunked ignored the job's exclude_paths entirely: it never applied shouldExcludeMount (so a whole-mount exclusion like /rootfs was skipped) and never mapped per-volume globs into the chunk walk. A container that bind-mounts the host root (Glances, Telegraf, Netdata: / → /rootfs) therefore had its entire host filesystem content-chunked into the dedup repo despite a /rootfs exclusion – slow runs, a bloated repo, and unrelated host files (boot/, lib64/, mnt/cache/appdata/…) appearing in the restore-point file list. The chunked path now reads exclude_paths, skips excluded mounts wholesale (recorded as skipped volumes), and passes volume-relative patterns through to the walk. FolderHandler.BackupChunked (used directly for folder/plugin dedup jobs and for each container volume) now applies the same shouldExcludePath filter the tar path uses – a matching directory is pruned (SkipDir) and never traversed. Classic tar backups were already correct; only the dedup path was affected.
  • Running dedup backups no longer display "-1%" in the Dashboard progress list. The daemon emits -1 as an "indeterminate progress" sentinel during the streaming chunk walk (total size isn't known up front). The per-item progress bar rendered this literally as a "-1%" label and a negative-width bar. Negative percent is now treated as indeterminate: the bar pulses at full width and the numeric label shows ··· until a real percentage arrives.
  • "Include in DB backup" toggle on the Storage page now persists. Two coordinated bugs hid behind the toast. (1) UpdateStorageDestination did not include backup_database_enabled in its UPDATE clause, so the DB silently dropped the field. (2) The storage PUT handler decodes into a partial-patch struct that omitted the field, so the request body's value was thrown away before even reaching the DB. Both were corrected.
  • retry_max_override and retry_delays_override (job edit) + retry_of_run_id / retry_next_at (job runs) now serialise as native JSON null / number / string instead of {"Valid":false,"Int64":0} wrapper objects. The override-retry input previously showed "[object Object]" with an "Invalid JSON" error because the form bound the wrapper struct directly. Backend struct fields are now pointer types (*int64, *string, *time.Time) so database/sql round-trips nullables transparently and the JSON encoder emits clean values.
  • Activity log details render duration as 1 min, 2.0 s, 7 min 10 s etc. instead of raw 60002ms / 430s. A new formatDuration helper in Logs.svelte handles both duration_ms and duration_seconds detail keys.

  • Retry policy delays are no longer a JSON textbox. Both Settings → Retry Policy and Job edit → Override retry policy now use a friendly editor: preset dropdown (Default 15 m / 1 h / 4 h, Aggressive 1 m / 5 m / 15 m, Patient 1 h / 6 h / 24 h, Custom) plus per-row [number] [unit ▾] rows with + Add / × Remove. The override section adds a "Use global default" checkbox that hides the editor and emits an empty value (= NULL on save).

  • S3-compatible uploads (MinIO, MEGA, IDrive E2, Backblaze B2 via S3) no longer fail with 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch when the job name contains spaces or other URL-reserved characters. The aws-sdk-go-v2 + custom endpoint resolver + path-style combo has a signing-vs-sending URL-encoding asymmetry that breaks every PutObject and DeleteObject for keys containing reserved characters. TestConnection (HeadBucket) keeps passing because it has no path beyond the bucket – the "test passes, every upload fails" fingerprint. The S3 adapter now sanitizes each key path segment to the RFC 3986 unreserved set before sending to the SDK. Both Write and Read use the same translation, so existing backups continue to restore and new backups produce sanitized keys that all gateways accept (closes follow-ups on #88).

  • S3 PutObject no longer attaches a CRC32 SigV4 trailer that breaks S3-compatible gateways. The 2026.05.02 fix set the global RequestChecksumCalculation=WhenRequired but the upload-layer client hard-codes its own CRC32 default, so the trailer was attached anyway. The S3 adapter now uses the stable feature/s3/manager.Uploader, which honours the global setting correctly. Multipart PartSize binding (640 GB → 10 TB per-object ceiling for large streams) is preserved.
  • Container backups for containers that bind-mount the host root (Glances, Telegraf, Netdata, cAdvisor, node-exporter with / → /rootfs) no longer recursively walk the host filesystem before the volume is skipped. The 2026.05.01 fix moved the exclusion check above the per-volume backup branch, but the auto-compression-downgrade pre-scan still ran on the bind-mount source first – a full filepath.Walk of the host root. A Test Containers job that took 37 s before regressed to 14 minutes. The exclusion check now genuinely runs first; the compression pre-scan only touches volumes that will actually be archived. Same job is back to 38 s.
  • PUT /api/v1/storage/{id} no longer destroys the destination when the caller sends a partial body. The handler was decoding into a fresh struct and writing the whole row, so a request like {"config":"..."} blanked name, type, and dedup_enabled and orphaned every job pointing at the destination. It now loads the existing row, merges only the fields explicitly provided, and rejects attempts to change immutable fields (type, dedup_enabled) with HTTP 400.
  • POST /api/v1/storage no longer leaks the plaintext password / S3 secret key in its 201 response. Get() redacted the config blob but Create() echoed the request body verbatim – credentials were visible in browser devtools' Network tab during Add Storage. Both Create() and Update() now re-fetch the persisted row and apply the same redaction.
  • POST /api/v1/storage now validates the type and config before persisting. Previously accepted arbitrary types ({"type":"bogus"} was 201-ed) and empty configs that could never construct a working adapter. Both Create() and Update() now build the adapter up-front and return HTTP 400 on construction failure with the underlying error.
  • POST /api/v1/jobs and PUT /api/v1/jobs/{id} now include the persisted items in their response so callers can chain on the server-assigned item IDs. Job fields stay at the top level for backwards compatibility (result.id still works).
  • GET /api/v1/storage/{id}/jobs returns the list of dependent jobs, not just a scalar count. Response now includes a jobs array of {id, name} so the UI can show which jobs would be orphaned by a delete. job_count is preserved.
  • GET /api/v1/storage/{id}/dedup-stats no longer returns 500 on a freshly-created dedup destination that hasn't run a backup yet. The Storage card now renders "0 chunks · 0 packs" instead of a broken-card state until real stats start flowing.
  • GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/restore-points/{rpid}/contents?item=… now works on dedup restore points instead of returning 500. The handler previously expected a per-item tar archive directory; dedup destinations don't have one. It now synthesizes the file list from the dedup manifest's per-file metadata so the restore-wizard file picker works for both classic and dedup restore points.
  • Recovery page no longer flags items as Unprotected when their owning job is disabled. The recovery API correctly reports has_restore_point: true regardless of the parent job's enabled flag, but the Svelte page derived its own protected set from enabled jobs only, so disabling a schedule (a common manual-only workflow) made items appear unprotected even though their backups were intact. The page now derives protection from has_restore_point directly, matching the API. The Dashboard's matching logic was updated the same way.
  • Recovery plan step status now considers every item, not just the first. The handler previously checked only items[0] to badge a step "ready" or "warning"; a step with one missing restore point but several intact ones was shown as ready. It now downgrades to "warning" if any item is missing.
  • Restore wizard file picker no longer hangs on "Loading…" after expanding "Restore specific files". The per-item state was held in a SvelteMap whose value objects were mutated directly after an await boundary – SvelteMap doesn't propagate mutations across awaits, so the UI never received the loading: false flip. The picker now writes a fresh object reference on every transition.
  • Folder/Plugin Items wizard step no longer falsely flags every custom folder as "Not found". The stale-detection check compared selected items against /api/v1/folders, which only returns engine-discoverable presets like the Flash Drive – so any user-added custom folder appeared "not found" even when the path was perfectly valid. A new GET /api/v1/path-exists?path=… endpoint does a safepath-validated os.Stat; the picker now async-checks every custom folder's path on mount and only flags it when the stat actually fails. The empty-state message was also rewritten to point users at the "Add Custom Folder" workflow instead of looking like an error.
  • Dedup stats endpoint now reports correct totals across daemon restarts and from any goroutine. Stats() previously returned in-memory counters that only the writing process saw, so the Storage card showed zeros after a restart. It now reads totals from SQL aggregates and derives logical bytes from restore_points.size_bytes summed over the destination's live dedup restore points.
  • GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/history and /restore-points return [] (not JSON null) for jobs with no rows. Front-end code that called .length or .map() on the response was throwing.
  • GET /api/v1/activity?limit=N clamps limit to ≤ 1000 to prevent an authenticated caller (or misconfigured monitor) from OOM-ing the daemon by requesting a huge limit.
  • WebSocket origin patterns now cover the entire RFC 1918 172.16.0.0/12 range (172.16.x.x through 172.31.x.x). Previously only 172.16.*.* was listed, so users on 172.17.0.0/16 (Docker's default network) through 172.31.x.x never received progress updates.
  • Password inputs across Settings, Storage, Restore wizard, and Replication forms now declare appropriate autocomplete attributes so browsers stop offering inappropriate suggestions and the verbose DOM warning on focus goes away.
  • Failed backup jobs no longer leave orphaned partial uploads at the destination. When the upload retry loop exhausted (or hit a verify mismatch or context cancellation), the runner returned without cleaning up the per-item files it had already written, wasting remote quota and confusing the next run. It now best-effort deletes every partial file before surfacing the error.
  • WebDAV chunk uploads use exponential backoff with HTTP-status-aware retry classification. Chunk PUTs retry on 423 Locked, 409 Conflict, 429 Too Many Requests, any 5xx, stall-watchdog timeouts, and transport errors (100ms → 300ms → 1s → 3s → 8s, 6 attempts). Permanent 4xx failures (401, 403, 404, 413, …) fail fast on the first attempt instead of consuming the full retry budget.
  • WebDAV uploads no longer buffer non-seekable backup streams into memory or leave encryption goroutines alive after stalled retries. Bounded objects use WriteStreamWithLength so the fallback that copies unknown-length streams into RAM is avoided (closes #96).
  • Large WebDAV backups are split into manifest-backed chunks instead of one monolithic PUT. Files larger than the configured WebDAV chunk size upload as independent fixed-size objects with per-chunk SHA-256 hashes and a manifest written last. Restore, verify, list, stat, and delete are manifest-aware while older single-file WebDAV backups remain readable (closes #97).
  • Importing dedup backups from another Vault instance now produces restorable restore points. manifest.json written to storage didn't include per-item dedup manifest IDs, and the import path didn't read them either – so re-discovered dedup backups appeared in the UI but the restore would fail because the chunks were unreachable. writeManifest now embeds item_manifests for dedup runs, and ImportBackups reads the field back, persisting per-item IDs in the restore-point metadata and promoting the ID onto the row directly for single-item dedup jobs. Non-dedup imports are unchanged. Manifests written before this change still import as classic file-based restore points (no regression).
  • Dead code cleanup: Server.Start, SettingsHandler.RestorationInfo, Client.GetJob, Syncer.SetHub, parseDomainDisks/domainDiskPaths, and decompressReader/fileCompressionExt removed. Each was either superseded by a context-aware variant, replaced by a content-based equivalent, or had no callers in the live tree.
  • Daemon now flushes the DB snapshot to USB flash after every config mutation, not just on startup/shutdown. Server.SetConfigChangeHook stored the hook on the Server struct but never forwarded it to the per-handler onConfigChange fields, so every notifyConfigChange() call across the four CRUD handlers was a no-op. The Server now stashes references to all four handlers and propagates the hook. StorageHandler and ReplicationHandler gained the missing hook plumbing too – every Create/Update/Delete now triggers the flush.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Folder dedup restore now validates every manifest path against the destination root before writing. FolderHandler.RestoreChunked joined every manifest entry to destPath with filepath.Join, which does not prevent .. segments from escaping the target directory. A tampered manifest at the storage destination could therefore have caused the restore to write files outside the chosen recovery folder (CWE-22 / CodeQL go/path-injection). Every entry now goes through safepath.JoinUnderBase, which rejects any path that wouldn't stay inside destPath. Closes CodeQL alerts #32–#35.
  • Pack writer now bounds its pre-allocation size. The pack-flush path allocated a buffer sized by bufLen + footerLen + 4 without an explicit cap. In practice these values are bounded by PackTargetSize (24 MiB) plus one chunk's slop, but CodeQL go/allocation-size-overflow couldn't see that. An explicit ceiling (PackTargetSize * 4) is now enforced with a clear error if exceeded. Closes CodeQL alert #37.
  • Discord-webhook log redaction now anchors on the https:// scheme prefix so it only matches genuine webhook URLs, not arbitrary log text that happens to mention the substring discord.com/api/webhooks/…. Behavioural impact is nil for real logs (the existing test still passes) but the regex now satisfies CodeQL go/regex/missing-regexp-anchor. Closes CodeQL alert #36.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• S3 / Backblaze B2 uploads of multi-GB objects no longer abort with context deadline exceeded mid-multipart (closes #95). The S3 adapter previously routed every operation – including large multipart uploads via transfermanager.Uploader – through a single hardcoded 5-minute context (ctxOp). A real Immich-style folder backup to Backblaze B2 exceeded that ceiling well before the upload (and its in-flight AbortMultipartUpload cleanup) could complete, producing a cascading context-cancellation failure. Upload operations are now scoped to a separate, configurable deadline (uploadTimeout, default 240 minutes / 4 hours) while metadata operations (Read / List / Stat / Delete / TestConnection) continue to use the existing 5-minute budget unchanged. A new optional upload_timeout_minutes field on the S3 storage config – surfaced in the Storage form as "Upload timeout (minutes)" under the existing advanced options – lets users tune the ceiling for very large files over slow links (set 0 to accept the 4-hour default; negative values are rejected at construction time).
  • Restored Docker containers now keep their port mappings – Unraid's "Container Port" and "LAN IP:Port" columns no longer go blank after a restore. Container backups capture Config.ExposedPorts and HostConfig.PortBindings from docker inspect, but the restore path declared a local portBindings map and immediately discarded it (_ = portBindings // avoid unused variable) without ever populating it from the inspect data or assigning it to the new container.HostConfig. Restored containers were therefore created with zero exposed ports and zero host-port bindings, which is exactly what Unraid's Docker page renders as a blank port column. The user could "fix" the row by clicking Edit → Done because Unraid then rebuilds the container from the on-disk template XML, masking the bug. The restore engine now converts both maps into the typed network.PortSet and network.PortMap the Docker API requires (parsing keys with network.ParsePort and netip.ParseAddr, skipping malformed entries with a log line), and assigns them to containerConfig.ExposedPorts and hostConfig.PortBindings respectively. Empty/invalid HostIP values are left as the zero netip.Addr so Docker treats them as "bind on all interfaces", matching its own default. Restored containers now show their port mappings immediately, with no Edit→Done dance required.
  • Restored Docker containers now show their correct update status in the Unraid Docker Manager UI instead of "not available". Unraid computes a container's "up-to-date" / "update available" badge by reading RepoDigests[0] from each image's metadata, but docker load (used during restore) does not populate RepoDigests – only docker pull does. As a result, restored containers showed "not available" and the "Check for Updates" button could not resolve a local digest, leaving the badge stuck. The container engine now captures each image's RepoDigests at backup time into a small image_meta.json companion file (alongside image.tar*), and the restore path uses that to re-seed /var/lib/docker/unraid-update-status.json with the recorded local digest after ImageLoad. The Unraid UI then resolves "up-to-date" or "update available" immediately, and "Check for Updates" works against the restored container. Verified end-to-end on Unraid against the "Test Containers" job: Grafana, Influxdb, and telegraf all flipped from "not available" to "up-to-date" after a fresh backup→restore cycle.
  • Restore now also performs a docker pull after ImageLoad to authoritatively populate RepoDigests for the restored image. This handles the chicken-and-egg case where the source container's image itself had no RepoDigests at backup time (e.g. the image was previously restored from tar without ever being pulled, or the user is upgrading from a Vault version older than the image_meta.json capture), in which case the backup's image_meta.json recorded repo_digests: null and the prior unraid-update-status.json seeder had nothing to write. The pull is non-destructive – when layers already exist locally (the common case immediately after ImageLoad) Docker only fetches the manifest, which is exactly the metadata required. The freshly-pulled digest is then written directly into unraid-update-status.json, so the badge flips to "up-to-date" without depending on the backup's recorded metadata. If the daemon is offline or the registry is unreachable, the call fails silently and the path falls back to image_meta.json-based seeding. Verified end-to-end on Unraid: nicolargo/glances:latest (which had empty RepoDigests on the host from a prior tar-only restore) flipped from "not available" to "up-to-date" after restore-with-pull.
  • Container Path Exclusions now skip directory bind mounts at the volume level (closes #70). The earlier fix (2026.05.01) only applied exclusion patterns to single-file bind mounts. Directory mounts – most notably the recursive / → /rootfs mount used by Telegraf, Netdata, cAdvisor, Glances, and Prometheus node-exporter – still entered the recursive walk and only filtered special-file inodes, so the engine eventually started archiving the host filesystem (including the array into itself) and the job hung indefinitely. Exclusion matching now runs once, up front, against every bind mount's container-side destination regardless of whether the mount is a file or a directory, mirroring the single-file behaviour the user reported as working. Verified end-to-end on Unraid with a real "Test Containers" job (Influxdb + Grafana + Glances + Telegraf, both Glances and Telegraf bind-mounting / → /rootfs): job completed in 37 s (4/4 items, 1.9 GB) with engine: skipping volume / … matches exclusion pattern in the daemon log, replacing a previous 13 m 37 s hang that failed at 2/4 items.
  • Compression setting now controls the actual on-disk archive format. Previously the engine always emitted gzip-wrapped tar archives while the runner additionally wrapped the upload stream with whatever compression the user selected, so jobs configured for zstd shipped double-compressed volume_*.tar.gz.zst files and jobs configured for None still produced .tar.gz. The engine (internal/engine/container.go, folder.go, plugin.go) is now the single source of truth for archive compression and emits .tar, .tar.gz, or .tar.zst per BackupItem.Compression, while the runner's upload path no longer wraps the stream a second time. Restore auto-detects the format via magic bytes (0x1f 0x8b for gzip, 0x28 0xb5 0x2f 0xfd for zstd, plain otherwise) and the engine looks up archives by trying base, base+".gz", and base+".zst" in turn, so existing .tar.gz backups (and legacy double-wrapped .tar.gz.zst files via the runner-side decompressStoredReader) continue to restore correctly. Verified end-to-end on Unraid against the "Test Containers" job: none → .tar, gzip → .tar.gz, zstd → .tar.zst.
  • Restore wizard "Choose Version" step now shows the absolute date alongside the relative offset inline (closes #81 follow-up from @SebboGit). The previous fix relied on a native title tooltip to surface the relative time on hover, but native browser tooltips were unreliable on the parent button row (Firefox in particular suppresses them when the <span> lives inside a role="button"/cursor: pointer ancestor). Both forms are now rendered together as 12 May 2026, 02:09 am · 7h ago, giving an unambiguous absolute timestamp with the relative offset always visible – no hover required, works on touch.
  • Logs page no longer collapses expanded "Details" rows every 5 s during auto-refresh. loadLogs() previously called expandedIds.clear() on every poll cycle and re-added only error rows, so any non-error row a user had manually expanded was wiped on the next refresh. The expanded set is now preserved across reloads, entries that have aged out of the visible window are pruned, and the auto-expand-error behaviour now tracks a separate "already auto-expanded" set so collapsing an auto-expanded error keeps it collapsed.
  • Failed backup jobs no longer leave orphaned partial uploads at the storage destination. When uploadStagedFiles exhausted its 4-attempt retry loop (or hit a verify mismatch or ctx cancellation), it returned an error without cleaning up the per-item files it had already successfully uploaded, or the partially-written bytes from the failing item. This wasted remote-storage quota (especially painful on quota-bounded providers like Hetzner Storage Box) and made the destination directory look "half done" to the next run. The runner now performs best-effort adapter.Delete() on every known partial file before returning the error. Cleanup failures are logged but never mask the original upload error.

  • WebDAV uploads of multi-GB files no longer fail with context deadline exceeded ... Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers (closes #83 follow-up from @SebboGit). The WebDAV adapter previously called gowebdav.Client.SetTimeout(60*time.Second), which maps to http.Client.Timeout – a single deadline that covers the entire request lifetime, including the upload body. A 20-container backup to Hetzner Storage Box repeatedly failed during the upload-retry loop (4× exponential-backoff attempts per item, all timing out at the same 60 s mark), eventually crashing the daemon. The fixed 60 s deadline is replaced with phase-specific http.Transport timeouts that do not bound body-transfer duration:

  • TCP dial 30 s, TCP keepalive 30 s

  • TLS handshake 30 s
  • Expect-Continue 5 s
  • Response headers 5 min (applies AFTER the body is fully sent)
  • Idle keep-alive 90 s
  • http.Client.Timeout left at 0 (unlimited) by default

In addition, every upload reader is now wrapped in a stall watchdog: it records the timestamp of every successful Read() and aborts the PUT with webdav: upload stalled when no bytes flow for the configured window (default 300 s / 5 min). Slow-but-progressing transfers of any size succeed; truly dead connections still fail promptly without depending on the OS keepalive.

  • Restore no longer fails with invalid input: magic number mismatch for backups produced by the new engine-side compression path. After the compression refactor that made the engine the single source of truth for archive compression, the runner stopped transport-wrapping uploads but the restore path's decompressStoredReader still blindly applied job.Compression to every downloaded file. That caused plain artifacts like config.json to be force-fed into a zstd reader during the restore of any zstd-mode job, producing downloading Test Containers/.../Glances/config.json: invalid input: magic number mismatch and aborting the run at 0/N items. decompressStoredReader is now content-based – it peeks the first four bytes and only strips a layer when the leading bytes actually match the gzip (0x1f 0x8b) or zstd (0x28 0xb5 0x2f 0xfd) magic, ignoring both the filename extension and the job's compression setting. This still strips one transport layer from legacy double-wrapped backups while leaving newly produced plain files (config.json, manifest.json, image.tar) untouched. Verified end-to-end on Unraid: a fresh zstd backup of 4 containers (Influxdb + Grafana + Glances + telegraf, 575 MB) restored in 1 s with 4/4 items succeeded, replacing the previous 1-failed/0-done error.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Image metadata capture (image_meta.json) is now written next to each container's image.tar* during backup. Stores image_tag and repo_digests so the engine can repopulate Unraid's docker unraid-update-status.json on restore (see Fixed). Old backups without this file fall back to current behaviour silently; the file is best-effort and never fails a backup.
  • Backup Size Trend chart on the History page is now coloured by backup target category. Each run is rendered as a bar tinted by its dominant item type – Containers (blue), VMs (purple), Folders & Files (green), Flash (amber), Other (gray) – with a top-right legend that doubles as a category filter. The hover tooltip shows the category swatch alongside the run's size, date, and job name, making it easy to see at a glance whether a size spike came from a container-heavy run, a VM snapshot, or a folder backup. The linear-regression trend indicator (Growing / Stable / Shrinking) is preserved. Job categories are derived from the dominant item_type across each job's items, hydrated via parallel getJob calls when the History page loads.
  • Helper text under the Compression dropdown in the Job wizard. Each option now surfaces a one-line trade-off summary so users can choose deliberately: None (fastest, zero CPU overhead, best for already-compressed media), Gzip (universal compatibility, moderate ratio/speed), Zstd (recommended; better compression than gzip and ~3–5× faster).
  • Two new optional WebDAV config fields exposed in the Storage form under "Advanced · Timeouts":
  • timeout_seconds – overall hard ceiling on every WebDAV request including upload body. Default 0 = unlimited (recommended). Power users can set a value if they want a strict per-request cap.
  • stall_timeout_seconds – abort an upload if no bytes flow for this many seconds. Default 300 (5 min). Set to a negative value to disable the watchdog entirely.
  • Recommended-exclusion presets for host-mount monitoring agents and Docker-socket-consuming management containers. Adds curated ContainerExclusionPresets entries for Telegraf, Glances, Netdata, cAdvisor, Prometheus node-exporter, Scrutiny, Prometheus, Loki, VictoriaMetrics, Uptime Kuma, Watchtower, Diun, Dozzle, Autoheal, Dockhand, and docker-socket-proxy, and enhances the existing Portainer preset to include /var/run/docker.sock. Telegraf and Glances now ship with /rootfs//hostfs//var/run/docker.sock (and friends) so the "Load recommended exclusions" button on the Container Path Exclusions step auto-populates the exact paths needed to prevent the recursive host-filesystem walk described in #70. The existing Svelte UI flow (fetchContainerPresets() → GET /api/v1/presets/exclusions?image=...) picks up the new presets automatically – no UI change required. Verified end-to-end on Unraid: clicking the button on the Test Containers job's Glances item populated /rootfs, /var/run/docker.sock, /etc/os-release (3 paths) and on the telegraf item populated /rootfs, /hostfs, /var/run/docker.sock, /var/run/utmp, /run/udev (5 paths), with both buttons flipping to the disabled "Recommended exclusions loaded" state.
  • /var/run/docker.sock and any other socket bind mounts are now auto-suggested as exclusions even when no image preset matches. The presets API (GET /api/v1/presets/exclusions) now accepts an optional container=<name_or_id> query parameter alongside image=. When provided, the daemon inspects the live container via the Docker SDK and appends every bind-mount destination whose host source ends in .sock (e.g. /var/run/docker.sock, /var/run/docker-shim.sock) to the recommended exclusions, deduplicated against the static image preset list. The job editor's "Container Path Exclusions" panel now passes the container name, so any container mounting a runtime socket gets the exclusion auto-populated without anyone having to maintain a per-image preset entry. Inspect failures are silently ignored so the editor still falls back to the static image preset list.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • Renamed the internal helper shouldExcludeFileMount to shouldExcludeMount and hoisted the call above the IsDir() dispatch in ContainerHandler.Backup() so it covers both directory and file mounts.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: • Bumped Go toolchain to 1.26.3 and golang.org/x/net to v0.53.0 to address two govulncheck findings. GO-2026-4971 (net: panic in Dial/LookupPort on Windows when handling NUL bytes – stdlib, fixed in Go 1.26.3) and GO-2026-4918 (HTTP/2 transport infinite loop on bad SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE – both stdlib and golang.org/x/net, fixed in Go 1.26.3 / x/net v0.53.0). make security-check (gosec + govulncheck + go mod verify) is now clean: 0 gosec issues, 0 vulnerabilities, all modules verified.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• VM checkpoint creation now succeeds for cold (shut-off) backups. Previously the engine called DomainCheckpointCreateXML against the persistent domain handle after restoreDomainState() had already destroyed the transient paused session – libvirt rejected the call with "Operation not supported: cannot create checkpoint for inactive domain", so every cold incremental/differential ran without ever recording a parent checkpoint and silently fell back to producing a full-size qcow2. Checkpoints are now created against the live (paused) backupDom while the transient backup session is still active, and only after the bitmap is persisted to qcow2 does the runner tear the session down. End-to-end verified against a cold Fedora VM: full = 2.3 GB, incremental and differential = 192 KB on a no-change cycle.
  • Engine no longer reports "incremental" / "differential" when no parent checkpoint is recorded. When the runner had no checkpoint metadata to pass (first run after a chain reset), the engine still produced a full-size backup but labelled the result vm_backup_type: incremental, which corrupted the chain bookkeeping. The fall-back logic now also covers the empty-parent case and downgrades actualType to "full" with a clear log entry before writing vm_meta.json and result.Meta.
  • VM incremental backups now actually capture only changed blocks. Previously every "incremental" or "differential" run silently produced a full copy of each qcow2 disk: the engine emitted a regular libvirt push-mode backup XML with no <incremental> element, and the only "incremental" behaviour was a file-mtime gate that either (a) re-copied the whole disk anyway when the VM was running (mtime always advanced) or (b) skipped the disk entirely when the VM was cold (mtime unchanged after the previous backup) – silently losing data. The engine now creates a libvirt checkpoint (persistent dirty bitmap stored in qcow2) after each successful backup and references it via <incremental>parent_checkpoint</incremental> on subsequent runs, so libvirt streams only the dirty blocks since the parent checkpoint. Restore points record the checkpoint name in vm_checkpoints metadata; missing-parent or non-qcow2 disks fall back to a full backup with a clear log entry. Retention cleanup deletes orphaned libvirt checkpoints. (closes the broken VM Incremental / Differential modes)
  • Backups failing with No space left on device when staging to /mnt/addons (1 MB tmpfs). The pool-discovery cascade in internal/unraid/pools.go selected any directory that exists under /mnt/, which on modern Unraid includes the /mnt/addons tmpfs mount. Pool discovery now reads /proc/self/mountinfo and rejects paths backed by tmpfs, devtmpfs, ramfs, proc, sysfs, cgroup, cgroup2, or overlay filesystems, so staging falls through to a real cache or array pool.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• VM chain restore for incremental and differential backups. The runner now stages each chain step into its own subdirectory and uses qemu-img rebase -u plus qemu-img convert -O qcow2 to materialise a single self-contained qcow2 per disk before invoking the existing libvirt restore path. The qemu-img invocation lives in the runner package to preserve the engine package's pure-Go invariant.
  • BackupResult.Meta channel for engine-specific metadata. The VM engine populates it with vm_checkpoint, vm_backup_type, and (when applicable) vm_parent_checkpoint, which the runner persists into restore-point metadata so future backups can locate their parent checkpoint and retention can clean up libvirt-side state.
  • VM vm_meta.json sidecar now records BackupType, Checkpoint, ParentCheckpoint, and per-disk Disks[] entries (Target, BackupFile, Format) for diagnostics and forward compatibility.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • Removed the legacy mtime-based changed_since gate from the VM backup path. Folder and container backups continue to use it. ZFS keeps its dataset-snapshot-based incremental flow unchanged.

docs.title: Verified
docs.text:
• Hot-VM backups end-to-end on a running Fedora guest: Full = 2.34 GB / 34 s (vault-run-6), Incremental from prior run = 3.5 MB / 1 s (vault-run-7), Differential from last full = 4.07 MB / 1 s (vault-run-8). All three runs created persistent libvirt checkpoints on the live (paused) backup session.
  • VM chain restore end-to-end: restored Fedora from incremental RP 7 (parent = full RP 6) using qemu-img rebase -u + qemu-img convert. The runner staged both layers, materialised a single 2.18 GiB self-contained qcow2, the engine redefined the domain and auto-started it, and the guest kernel booted successfully (balloon driver active, vCPUs accumulating CPU time).

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Defer remote upload mode for slow-link backups (closes #77). New per-job toggle "Defer remote upload until all backups complete" stages every container backup to local disk first, restarts all containers as soon as staging is done, then streams the staged archives to the remote destination in a second phase. Containers go offline only for the (fast) local backup window, while the (slow) remote upload runs while every service is back online. The toggle is disabled when the destination is local (no benefit) and is automatically gated behind a non-local dest.Type. Per-file uploads are now retried up to 3 times with exponential backoff (5s → 30s → 2m), recovering automatically from transient remote-storage failures that previously failed entire jobs. WebSocket backup_phase, item_staged, and item_upload_start events drive a STAGING / UPLOADING phase indicator in the Backup Progress panel. Schema migration adds a defer_remote_upload column to jobs (default off). v1 scope: containers only – VM/folder/plugin/zfs items continue to upload inline.
  • WebDAV storage backend (closes #83). Stateless HTTP-based backup target that avoids per-user concurrent-connection limits seen on managed SFTP/SMB providers. Supports Basic and Digest auth (negotiated automatically), optional self-signed TLS, and an optional base path. Compatible with Nextcloud, ownCloud, Synology WebDAV, and any RFC 4918 server.
  • S3 / S3-compatible storage backend (closes #88). Built on AWS SDK v2 with a reusable, connection-pooled client. Works with AWS S3, Backblaze B2, MinIO, Cloudflare R2, and Wasabi via configurable endpoint and force-path-style options. Uses the SDK's manager.Uploader for streaming uploads of arbitrarily large archives without buffering to disk.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • Restore wizard "Choose Version" step, the Restore page restore-point list, the Job History timeline, the Dashboard Recent Activity panel, and the Logs page now show absolute timestamps (e.g. Apr 21, 2026, 21:22) as the primary label on each row, with the relative form (48m ago, 2d ago) preserved as a hover tooltip. This matches how Veeam, restic, and Time Machine present restore points and aligns with established UX guidance: when the user is matching a backup to a remembered point in time ("this was working fine until 17 April"), an absolute date is far easier to scan than mentally subtracting a relative offset (closes #81)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• S3 storage adapter requests now correctly include the bucket name in the URL when a custom endpoint is configured (e.g., MinIO, Backblaze B2, Cloudflare R2, Wasabi). The custom EndpointResolverV2 previously returned the bare endpoint URI, which suppressed the AWS SDK v2's automatic bucket injection – every PutObject / GetObject / HeadBucket request landed on the root path and the server responded with NoSuchBucket. The resolver now injects the bucket into the URL path (path-style) or hostname (virtual-host style) itself, matching what the SDK does for the default AWS resolver. Confirmed end-to-end against MinIO via the new make test-cloud-storage smoke test (closes #88)
  • Add Storage modal: switching between storage types (SFTP/SMB/NFS → Local Path, etc.) now correctly tears down the previous type's fields. Previously, fields from the prior selection could persist after a type change due to Svelte 5 reusing DOM input nodes across the dynamic {#if} branches. Wrapped the dynamic config block in {#key form.type} so the entire field subtree is recreated on every type switch
  • Pool drive detection no longer falsely reports "No cache drive detected" when /mnt/cache exists as an unmounted directory or when the user's pool is named something other than cache. unraid.PreferredPool() now consults /proc/self/mountinfo (via the existing IsMountedPool() helper) and returns the first mounted pool from discovery instead of returning /mnt/cache whenever the directory is present. checkCacheMount() likewise uses IsMountedPool() rather than the previous "directory non-empty = mounted" heuristic, so empty-but-mounted pools are correctly recognised as available for hybrid mode. Daemon startup also now logs every discovered pool with its mount status to make this diagnosable from /var/log/syslog (closes #69)
  • New / Edit Job wizard no longer freezes on the second step when accessed over plain HTTP (e.g. http://<server>:81/plugins/vault/ui/...). The Tooltip component called crypto.randomUUID() unconditionally, but that API is only available in secure contexts (HTTPS or localhost); on plain HTTP, Firefox throws TypeError: crypto.randomUUID is not a function, which crashed every wizard step that mounts new tooltips (Schedule / Details / Advanced) while the stepper indicator still advanced. Tooltip now generates its fallback id with a Math.random()-based path when crypto.randomUUID is unavailable. The same fix also restores the SMB/CIFS Username/Password fields and the Settings page, which previously failed to render in Brave / Edge / Firefox over plain HTTP for the same reason. Closes #67, closes #82
  • Importing backups from a storage destination now restores the full job and per-item configuration, not just the job name and encryption type. The on-disk manifest.json is now versioned (v2) and persists per-item rows (name, type, id, settings) plus job-level settings (backup_type_chain, retention_count, retention_days, container_mode, vm_mode, notify_on, verify_backup). The Storage → Import flow uses these fields to recreate Vault's job_items rows so the restore wizard immediately lists each backed-up container/VM/folder. For older manifests without an items array, item names are inferred from item_sizes; appdata.backup imports create a single container item per file. Closes #75
  • Restore points, Dashboard Protection Status, and the Disaster Recovery plan no longer disappear when a job's schedule is disabled. Protection is now derived from whether items have actual restore points on disk, not from the enabled schedule flag – so disabling a schedule (e.g. for a one-off / manual-only backup workflow) keeps already-backed-up items visible and protected. Affects GET /api/v1/health/summary (protected_items / protection_pct), GET /api/v1/recovery/plan, and the Restore page job picker (closes #76)
  • Container backups no longer fail with archive/tar: sockets not supported when a container has a Unix domain socket bind-mounted (e.g. Dockhand mounting /var/run/docker.sock). The engine now (a) auto-skips bind mounts whose source is a non-regular inode (socket, named pipe, device, irregular) with a clear unsupported inode type skip reason, and (b) honours user-defined Container Path Exclusions for file-based bind mounts using the same pattern semantics as directory mounts – exact paths, parent directories, basenames, and globs (*docker.sock*, *.sock) all work as documented in the UI hint. Previously the file-mount branch ignored the exclusion list entirely (closes #70)
  • Stop and Restart buttons on Settings → Vault no longer fail with Vault service control failed (HTTP 403). The plugin's control.php was performing a redundant CSRF check, but Unraid's web framework already validates csrf_token at the gateway and strips it from $_POST before forwarding to PHP – so the in-script comparison always saw an empty token and returned 403. The redundant check has been removed; the gateway CSRF validation plus the POST-method requirement still protect the endpoint (closes #71)
  • Eliminated the dual-scrollbar layout bug on the Vault web UI Settings page (and any other tall page). html, body, and #app are now locked to the viewport height with overflow: hidden, so the SPA's <main> is the only scroll surface – the page's left navigation can no longer scroll out of view (closes #73)
  • Service Control on the Vault settings page no longer falsely reports "STOPPED" when a Stop/Restart action fails. The Stop and Restart buttons now use a conservative fallback (preserve the pre-action state on errors), surface an inline error message when the request fails or the rc script exits non-zero, and confirm the real outcome by polling the daemon after the action. The PHP is_running() helper now consults /api/v1/health (the same authoritative check used at page load) and only falls back to the PID file when the health endpoint is unreachable, so post-action status agrees with what the user sees on refresh (closes #71)
  • Plugin upgrades now stop the running Vault daemon before upgradepkg --install-new and restart it afterwards, so users get the new binary without needing to reboot Unraid. User configuration (vault.cfg), the database (vault.db), and sealed credentials under /boot/config/plugins/vault/ are preserved across upgrades (closes #72)
  • Settings and configuration are no longer lost on plugin upgrade. In hybrid mode the daemon now refreshes the USB safety-net (/boot/config/plugins/vault/vault.db.backup) immediately after a successful restoration at startup, so the recovery chain (configured snapshot → default cache snapshot → USB backup) always has a current entry – even if a previous daemon shutdown was unclean. Combined with the graceful pre-upgrade stop, this guarantees a fresh-database fallback can no longer happen silently during an upgrade (closes #74)
  • Storage adapter durability: LocalAdapter, SFTPAdapter, and SMBAdapter Write() now perform a checked Sync() (where supported) plus a checked Close() and remove the partial file on any error, instead of relying on a defer f.Close() whose error was swallowed. Previously a write that failed mid-stream – or a final Close() that returned an error from a buffered remote SMB/SFTP server – would leave a truncated file on the destination and report success to the caller.
  • Database restore endpoint hardening: POST /api/v1/storage/{id}/restore-db now validates storage_path, rejecting empty values and any payload containing ... The handler also propagates errors from closing the live DB, the source temp file, and the destination DB file – and now Sync()s the destination before declaring success, removing the partial file on any failure. Previously these errors were silently discarded.
  • Health score rounding: GET /api/v1/health/summary now rounds the weighted health score to the nearest integer instead of truncating, so a 99.6% score displays as 100 rather than 99.
  • Job history input validation: GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/history now returns HTTP 400 when limit is non-numeric or less than 1 instead of silently falling back to the default of 50.
  • Frontend listener registration: the hash-based router and theme module now guard against duplicate hashchange and prefers-color-scheme listeners under hot module reload, eliminating dev-mode listener leaks.
  • SFTP port input validation: the Storage modal port field now enforces min=1/max=65535, preventing accidental zero or negative values being stored.
  • Command palette error visibility: CommandPalette.svelte now logs listJobs / listStorage / runJob / testStorage failures via console.error instead of swallowing them silently, making palette malfunctions diagnosable from devtools.
  • S3 List timeout consistency: S3Adapter.List() now uses the shared ctxOp() helper instead of a divergent hardcoded 10-minute timeout, matching every other S3 operation.
  • Request logger guidance: added an explicit comment in internal/api/middleware.go enumerating which authorization headers must be redacted if header logging is ever added (Authorization, X-API-Key, Cookie, Set-Cookie, Proxy-Authorization), to prevent accidental credential leaks in future changes.
  • Emergency-kit download race: Settings.svelte now defers URL.revokeObjectURL() for one second after a.click() so slow disks/browsers don't lose the blob URL before the download starts.
  • Missing dynamix.cfg log warning: detectTimeFormatFromPath() now logs a warning when reading /boot/config/plugins/dynamix/dynamix.cfg returns an unexpected error (anything other than "file not found"), so silent fallbacks to auto are no longer invisible.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Fixed job creation wizard step indicator scrolling out of view on tall steps (e.g. step 3 with many schedule and storage fields) – the step indicator is now pinned in a non-scrolling band below the modal title, always visible regardless of scroll position
  • Fixed path browser breadcrumbs showing double slashes (e.g. //mnt instead of /mnt) when browsing server paths for storage and database locations
  • Added per-restore-point deletion: each restore point in the Restore wizard now has a trash button (two-click confirm) that deletes both the backup files from storage and the database record – closes the user request for "delete a backup without deleting the job"
  • Added subfolder field to the Import Backups modal on the Storage page – lets users point the scanner at a specific subdirectory when their AppData Backup archives are not at the storage root (e.g. appdata-backups/)
  • Fixed AppData Backup flash-backup detection to match any <hostname>-<date>.zip file instead of only cube-*.zip – works for systems named tower, unraid, or any other hostname
  • Fixed Backup Size Trend chart showing wildly incorrect percentages (e.g. +1120%) when multiple jobs are visible – switched from last-point comparison to linear regression; mixed-job views now show a directional label (Growing/Shrinking/Stable) instead of a misleading number, while single-job filtered views still show the exact percentage
  • Verified sequential job execution: 3 jobs queued simultaneously (Jackett, Mosquitto/Tailscale, Fedora VM) all completed in sequence without stalling – the reported "stops after 2 backups" issue does not reproduce on the current codebase
  • Fixed missing getAPIKeyStatus, generateAPIKey, and revokeAPIKey methods in the API client (api.js), which caused a console error on every Settings page load and always showed "No API key configured" regardless of actual state
  • Fixed undefined bg-accent/text-accent Tailwind v4 tokens on the "backup" type badge in History run rows – replaced with bg-vault/15 text-vault so the badge is now visible in both light and dark modes
  • Added aria-pressed state to all filter/segmented-control buttons in History and Logs pages, and wrapped filter groups in role="group" with descriptive aria-label for screen-reader usability
  • Added aria-current="page" to sidebar navigation and mobile bottom-nav buttons so the active page is announced by screen readers
  • Added aria-label to the search input on the History page
  • Changed mobile bottom-nav "More" button icon from a gear to a three-dots ellipsis, matching the standard convention for overflow menus
  • Added an active indicator dot beneath the current page icon in the mobile bottom navigation bar
  • Scoped the html theme transition (background-color/color) inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) to respect the OS reduced-motion accessibility setting
  • Added scroll-fade gradient hint on mobile Dashboard stats row to indicate horizontal scrollability
  • Replaced non-standard checkbox in Logs page auto-scroll control with a proper role="switch" toggle button matching the design pattern used throughout the Settings page
  • Removed duplicate action buttons on Jobs, Storage, and Replication pages – top-right header button now only appears when items exist, eliminating redundancy with the empty-state center button
  • Fixed nil pointer dereference on startup: BrowseHandler was not assigned to the server struct in setupRoutes, causing a panic when SetZFSLister was called
  • Fixed sync.Mutex deadlock in runner: RunJob already holds r.mu, removed redundant lock around snapshotManager access in snapshot save
  • Clipboard copy in Settings UI now handles errors with an error toast instead of silently failing
  • Middleware test SetSetting calls now check for errors to prevent misleading test results
  • API error responses no longer leak internal error details to clients; all 500 responses now return a generic "internal server error" message while the real error is logged server-side (OWASP A09)
  • SMB storage adapter now enforces a 30-second dial timeout via context.WithTimeout to prevent indefinite connection hangs
  • SFTP adapter logs a warning when falling back to InsecureIgnoreHostKey due to missing host key verification configuration
  • Runner SetSnapshotManager write is now protected by mutex to prevent a data race with concurrent job execution
  • SMB smbReadCloser.Close() now uses errors.Join to surface file/share/session close failures instead of silently discarding them
  • NFS adapter unmount() now logs errors from umount and temp directory removal instead of silently discarding them
  • Mirrored SSD cache pools (e.g. /mnt/cache2, /mnt/cache3) not detected under Settings → Database Location and Temporary Work Area – pool discovery now scans /mnt/ at runtime using exclusion-based filtering (closes #49)
  • Browse handler filesystem roots now dynamically discover all pool drives instead of relying on a hardcoded "Cache" entry
  • Path traversal vulnerability (CWE-22) in SnapshotManager – added validateSnapshotPath defense-in-depth validation to SaveSnapshot, SetSnapshotPath, RestoreFromSnapshot, RestoreFromPath, SetUSBBackupPath, and saveUSBBackup with .. component rejection before filepath.Clean + filepath.Abs normalisation; uses filepath.ToSlash for cross-platform traversal detection (closes #27, closes #28)
  • Data race in SaveSnapshot reading snapshotPath without mutex protection – now reads the field under lock consistently with other accessors
  • Diagnostics collector hybrid-mode detection now checks that the preferred pool is mounted (matching daemon startup behaviour) instead of only checking directory existence
  • CSRF token validation added to control.php for state-changing actions (start, stop, restart, reset-config) – token sourced exclusively from POST
  • IPv6 loopback (::1) bind address now connects via [::1] instead of 127.0.0.1 in the PHP proxy, fixing connectivity when the daemon binds exclusively to IPv6
  • Bind-address validation in apply.sh and rc.vault now uses grep -F (fixed-string) to prevent regex wildcard matching of IPv4 dots, and apply.sh accepts IPv6 loopback/wildcard (::1, ::)
  • apply.sh no longer sources the config file directly – safely extracts only the BIND_ADDRESS key via grep/sed to prevent arbitrary code execution from user-editable config
  • apply.sh now checks sed -i exit status and aborts with an error if the config update fails
  • INI sanitisation in control.php now strips backslashes in addition to quotes and newlines, preventing backslash-escape attacks on INI quoting
  • Tooltip clipping when positioned near viewport edges – switched from position: absolute to position: fixed with JS-calculated viewport coordinates and horizontal clamping
  • Container path exclusion presets now load correctly when Vault runs behind the Unraid web proxy; fetchContainerPresets() uses buildApiRequest() instead of raw fetch() to route through the authenticated proxy endpoint (closes #11)
  • Stuck backup jobs can no longer run indefinitely – timeout and stall detection ensure jobs are always bounded (closes #28)
  • Time format detection now falls back to [notify][time] in dynamix.cfg when [display][time] is absent, fixing detection on Unraid 7.x where the time format preference is stored in the notification settings section
  • Unraid Settings/Vault page was blank due to duplicated PHP code in api.php causing a syntax error; removed the corrupted duplicate block to restore the service control panel, Web UI button, and port/binding configuration
  • SMB and SFTP storage adapters now honour the "Path" field: frontend forms send base_path matching the backend struct, and adapters accept the legacy path JSON key as a fallback for backward compatibility (closes #25)
  • Job deletion with "Delete Backup Files" now properly removes empty directories after deleting their contents, fixing the issue where backup files and directories were left on Local and SMB storage (closes #26)
  • SMB adapter Write() now propagates MkdirAll errors instead of silently ignoring them
  • ItemPicker selected-items map wrapped in $state() to ensure Svelte 5 reactive tracking (closes #22)
  • Items deleted from Unraid (containers, VMs, folders, plugins) can now be removed from backup jobs via the new remove button in the Backup Order list; stale items that no longer exist on the system are visually flagged with a "Not found" warning indicator (closes #24)
  • Storage form "Save" button now guards against double-submission with a saving flag and shows a "Saving…" state while the request is in flight
  • Container volume backups now skip Unix sockets, character/block devices, and named pipes instead of failing with "sockets not supported" errors; affected containers (e.g. those mounting /var/run/docker.sock) will complete successfully with a log entry for each skipped special file (closes #5)
  • Monthly schedule day picker now shows all 31 days instead of only days 1–28; previously Array(27) omitted days 29, 30, and 31 (closes #9)
